Dear Ruslan,

We are reaching out to inform you of an issue concerning your Bolt account. On 19.02, we received a report from a different individual stating that he noticed that his Bolt account displayed information about another individual (you). Following this, our investigation determined the following:

* You originally created a Bolt account in 2022 (the “Account”) using a phone number ending in 9556 (the “Phone Number”), which we understand was previously yours.
* On 19th February 2025, we were informed that a different individual was able to log into your Account using the same phone number which now belongs to him. Because our system still recognised the Phone Number as a valid credential for accessing the Account, the individual was able to sign in without requiring additional authentication.

To resolve this issue, we *suspended* the Account in accordance with our internal policies, ensuring that the other person can no longer access it. Therefore, the issue should not longer persist and once we conclude the internal investigation of how the access had been obtained, the account will be scheduled for deletion in alignment with our retention and deletion policies.

To assist in verifying our findings, could you confirm whether you are currently using a different phone number from the one used to create the Account in 2022? If so, what was the approximate moment that you changed it?

 

If you have any questions or need further clarification, please let us know.

Sincerely,

Bolt

Whoever is going to handle this ticket, please consider changing the the way we activate business company promo code. Currently, in N+1 places we fire {{business_company_promo_code_activate}} event to SNS topic and we have a [consumer|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/src/business/core/business/main/internal/service/events/BusinessCompanyPromoCodeEventService.ts#L20] for this event which do certain actions while activating business company promo code. 

And that’s the problem. Currently we trigger this event when  company’s postpaid application is approved manually, company is converted to postpaid, or when promo code is added from portal, or CC company is activated. And now we have this hidden company being reactivated. We have missing part. In order to avoid from these kind of situations in the future, I would suggest to implement it properly with Kafka CDC. Simply, check for company state being active and trigger the event and the rest will be handled. Happy to discuss the details.

Hi [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] regarding your points: 

*_Will all FOs, regardless of their type (rental/employment etc) have this option? Why?_*

The idea is to provide this to all fleet owners. As in the RFC, It's more prevalent in the Hiring/Employment fleets, affecting about 30% (hiring), but it is  also present in Rental markets (around 20%); we aim to give the tool to all FOs so they can manage categories in their fleets, preventing drivers to opt-out from categories, especially the core ones (basic/bolt) which are 90% of the FR in most cases. 

*“**_Selected mandatory categories by fleet can’t be opted out by the driver_**” - does this mean that even if the driver provides legitimate reasons why he doesn’t want to be in a specific category anymore, we will not consider this?* 

The driver would have to negotiate that with the fleet owner when driving with a fleet. But in cases where core categories are opted out, what would be a legitimate reason? That’s the core intent of this feature: to prevent drivers from acting like this. 


*What if a driver changed the car and it no longer qualifies for the category?*

It will still be mandatory by the fleet but not applicable to this specific driver. Category control doesn’t override category rules.

{noformat}SELECT t.city_id||':'||t.order_id as key,
            1 as fraud_driver_gps_upfront
            FROM
            (
            WITH count_of_orders as (
            SELECT ot.driver_id,
            COUNT(distinct etl.order_id) as count_of_orders
            FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
            JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try ot ON etl.order_id = ot.order_id AND etl.city_id = ot.city_id
            WHERE  etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
                AND ot.state='finished'
                AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
                AND etl.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
            GROUP BY 1
            )
            SELECT etl.country_code,
            ot.driver_id,
            coo.count_of_orders,
            etl.order_id as order_id,
            etl.city_id AS city_id,
            etl.partner_price_eur,
            pp.predicted_price*1.0/r.rate as predicted_price,
            (pp.predicted_price-ot.ride_price)*1.00/NULLIF(ot.ride_price,0) as price_diff,
            --opc.metered_price/r.rate as meter_based_price,
            (opc.metered_price-etl.partner_price)*1.0/NULLIF(etl.partner_price,0) as meter_price_diff,
            ot.ride_distance,
            pp.distance as predicted_distance,
            (pp.distance-ot.ride_distance)*1.00/NULLIF(ot.ride_distance,0) as distance_diff,
            foc.ride_duration,
            pp.duration as predicted_duration,
            (pp.duration-foc.ride_duration)*1.00/NULLIF(foc.ride_duration,0) as duration_diff,
            (CAST(pp.distance AS double)/1000)/NULLIF((CAST(foc.ride_duration AS double)/3600),0) as fraud_speed_km_h,
            ROUND((SQRT(POWER(co.destination_lat-f.lat,2)+POWER(co.destination_lng-f.lng,2))*111)*1.0,1) as finishing_accuracy,
            DATEDIFF(second,etl.created,f.created) as order_duration,

            FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl 
            LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order AS co ON etl.order_id = co.id AND etl.city_id = co.city_id

            LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_state_log as f ON f.order_try_id=ot.id AND f.city_id=ot.city_id --AND f.to_state='finished'
            LEFT JOIN count_of_orders as coo ON coo.driver_id=ot.driver_id
            LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.currency_exchange_rates r ON DATE(r.valid_on) = DATE(etl.created) AND r.currency = ot.price_currency
            WHERE  etl.order_type = 'rides'
                AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
                AND ot.state='finished'
                AND ot.auto_finish_time IS NULL
                AND etl.payment_method_group = 'in-app'
                AND etl.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND etl.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND pp.type='upfront'
                AND ot.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND ot.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND foc.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                --AND foc.created_date_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -10, current_date) as date)
                AND pp.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND pp.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND opc.created >= DATEADD(day, -7, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND opc.created_date >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)
                AND f.to_state='finished'
                AND f.created >= DATEADD(day, -10, CURRENT_DATE)

This HAVING clause *filters out unusual ride pricing, duration mismatches, and suspiciously close rides* based on the following conditions:

# *Predicted vs. Actual Price Difference:*
## *Keeps rides where* the predicted price is within *±30%* of the actual ride price.
## *Excludes rides where* the predicted price is off by *more than 30%*.
# *Predicted vs. Actual Duration Difference:*
## *Keeps rides where* the predicted duration is at most *2×* the actual duration.
## *Excludes rides where* the predicted duration is *≥100% longer* than the actual duration.
# *Metered Price vs. Partner Price (Filtering Suspiciously Low Prices):*
## *Excludes rides where* the metered price is *>50% lower* than the partner price *and* the ride destination is *<1 km away*.
# *Ride Time and Speed Check (Filtering Unrealistic Speeds & Close Distances):*
## *Excludes rides where:*
### The actual ride duration is *longer than expected*.
### The ride speed is *>100 km/h*.
### The ride destination is *<0.1 km (100m) away*.

Hi! Correct me if I’m wrong, but the provided screenshots do not look like the tax summary? However, In the provided screenshots, rider discounts have already been added in. So for example, for the week of 13.01-19.01 the total earnings INCLUDING discounts compensated by Bolt is 41.6€ [in-app earnings] + 3.4€ [rider discounts comped by Bolt] = 45€. 

However, you will see on the screenshot I attached that it shows rider_discounts_netted. Netted means that we take the discounts provided off the commission owed to Bolt. So while the total commission owed for January is 93.71€ + 2€ = 95.71€, when we net 9€ of rider discounts from it, the driver only owes us 86.71€ which is the sum on the official commission invoice the driver receives. 

The reason it’s done this way is that it is actually more tax effective, for the driver as well, because instead of adding the amount of top of taxable earnings, we deduct it from amount owed to Bolt. 



Hope this clears it up!

I unblocked the archive jobs by altering the state directly into DB.
*What’s the cause*

* logs shows cron->run took exceeded timeout with a long running DB queries
* the system is designed to tolerate these situations by relying on the execution context state. Normally, it detects the marker that a state has been started but no feedback about the exit, and it decides to postpone the archiving
* what happened in this situation is the long running query was exactly the query that enables the next active task after the previous was already disabled
* it fails to enable the next task, and when the new cron->run executes it detects NO active tasks, and decides to stop the archive.



Potential Solution 

* review MultiTablePlanner state and check the need for more db transactions

Use case: You’re charged in Czechia the waiting fee. So you price spikes. You’re not panicking, because bank or ApplePay is not sending any text messages about the charge. 

But if you’re in Middle-East you will get these messages, so despite the automation and AI, you gonna freak out and send a CS ticket. 

It’s not about the DSAT, it’s about how we want to make it more understandable from the CS side in the Middle-East region and Mexico 🙂 And since the new automation was [approved,|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C064FCFAT0S/p1741783294457709] it would make sense to cover this also from the FAQ angle.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* Relates to Bolt Car Program in France. Intention is for Bolt to reach out to the drivers to inform them about the earnings they have received through the Program.
** Goal is to incentivise high performance by highlighting the benefits of the program, including potential rewards and bonuses.
* Additionally, Bolt wants to create a leaderboard-style system within the Bolt Car Program.
** This system would rank their performance and offer bonuses to reward them.
** Ranking would be anonymised to ensure driver privacy.

+*QUESTIONS*+

* Can we contact these drivers to inform them about the earnings *without their explicit consent*? If consent is required, how can we collect it in a compliant manner?
* Are there any legal *constraints when communicating performance-based incentives* tied to the Bolt Car Program?
* Can we implement a *leaderboard-style gamification system* for drivers, considering that the ranking would be anonymised?

+*ANALYSIS*+

* Communicating performance based-incentives:
** Localisation:
*** It is worth probing why exactly we are doing this in France, and not globally. {color:#ff5630}*We shy away from local solutions*{color}, and prefer to keep things uniform.
** Data to be shared:
*** We should {color:#ff5630}*only be sharing the data strictly needed*{color} for this purpose, particularly if it is sensitive (e.g., if we do not need to provide a full breakdown of their earnings, we should not do so). Otherwise, we are being disproportionate and intrusive.
** Legal basis:
*** Seems unlikely that we would require consent here. We are not promoting new / third-party services; we are instead informing drivers about their earnings. There is certainly a marketing element here (as we are highlighting the benefits of the Bolt Car Program), so the purpose would be marketing-related. However, consent not strictly required (soft opt-in would apply).
*** Instead, legitimate interest would be the applicable legal basis. Ideally we would conduct a {color:#36b37e}*Legitimate Interest Assessment*{color} for this. Add it to backlog ([https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1lyScH1kZNk1-FeUbmkAdOBDbmbuYkBACcCvwG6EuhF4/edit?gid=0#gid=0|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1lyScH1kZNk1-FeUbmkAdOBDbmbuYkBACcCvwG6EuhF4/edit?gid=0#gid=0|smart-link]).
** Transparency:
*** Not explicitly covered in the driver privacy notice, as not yet updated. However, this will be covered in the updated privacy notice (mostly likely under the marketing section).
*** {color:#ff5630}*Flag this as a compliance risk*{color}. Some {color:#4c9aff}*disclaimer wording*{color} may be appropriate.
**** e.g., “_[_{color:#ff5630}_Bolt_{color}_] shares this information with you based on our legitimate interest in promoting our services, in accordance with Article 6(1)(f) of the General Data Protection Regulation. For further information on how Bolt processes your personal data, including information on your data privacy rights, we refer you to our privacy notice available at:_ [_https://bolt.eu/fr-fr/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides_|https://bolt.eu/fr-fr/privacy/privacy-for-drivers/?category=rides]”
*** As this falls within the remit of a marketing period, identity of the sender must be clear. As such, if this is being sent by the {color:#4c9aff}*French Bolt entity*{color} (Bolt Services France SARL), we should list this.
** Security:
*** Given a complaint we received relating to HMRC data sharing, it would be worth sharing this information with {color:#4c9aff}*extra layers of security*{color} (e.g., an encrypted zip file, rather than in the body of the email).
** DSRRs:
*** We should ensure that users are {color:#4c9aff}*able to easily opt-out*{color} of receiving such emails. Ideally, we should include an unsubscribe functionality in the email itself; otherwise, we can rely on usual opt-out processes.
*** If any of the information is inaccurate, we need to make sure we {color:#4c9aff}*have a process for correcting*{color} it quickly. This is similar to what we have seen with HMRC reporting.
** Other considerations:
*** {color:#36b37e}*Check with GFT*{color} whether this creates any reclass risk. Seems they have already been looped in.
*** Ask for the specific {color:#4c9aff}*contents of the emai*{color}l, for completeness.
* Leaderboard:
** Localisation:
*** It is worth probing why exactly we are doing this in France, and not globally. {color:#ff5630}*We shy away from local solutions*{color}, and prefer to keep things uniform.
*** Is this a {color:#4c9aff}*MVRA project*{color}?
** Data / risk profile:
*** Primarily, we need a {color:#4c9aff}*PPRA*{color} completed on this, as we currently have no visibility on how this will work.
*** I appreciate that the ranking itself will be anonymised - this is good. However, presumably the data being fed in will not be - what is it? In particular, {color:#4c9aff}*how would we rank their performance*{color}? We should only use {color:#ff5630}*data that is strictly necessary*{color}.
*** {color:#36b37e}*DPIA*{color} likely needed here, as risk of exclusion from bonuses, profiling / scoring elements, etc.
** A22:
*** There is a risk that, by ranking performance and offering bonuses as a result, this {color:#ff5630}*could be considered A22 / profiling*{color}. More information is needed first.
*** If A22 applies, a way to de-risk this would be to maybe not offer the bonuses, or to offer {color:#4c9aff}*less substantial incentives*{color}. We also want to ensure the system is configured to {color:#4c9aff}*minimise biases*{color}, and there is {color:#4c9aff}*clear documentation*{color} in place explaining how decisions are made here (particularly to respond to DSARs).
** Purpose / legal basis:
*** Purpose would be motivate / incentivise drivers, which due to reclass risk is something we usually aim to avoid. Also, data proportionality would depend on what we are using to measure driver performance.
*** If we did proceed with it, the only legal basis that would apply is legitimate interest. As such a {color:#36b37e}*Legitimate Interest Assessment*{color} would be needed.
** Transparency:
*** We still need to know exactly what data we are using here.
*** Not explicitly covered in the driver privacy notice, as not yet updated. In any case, not included in the updated version either. This is a {color:#ff5630}*compliance gap*{color}. We could {color:#4c9aff}*prepare some PN language*{color} to cover this, but I would prefer GFT sign-off first given incentivisation.
** DSRRs:
*** We should ensure that there is a way for drivers to {color:#4c9aff}*opt-out*{color} of this, unless we have a good business reason for denying this.
** Other considerations:
*** {color:#36b37e}*Check with GFT*{color} whether this creates any reclass risk. Seems they have already been looped in.

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Ask the reporter:
** What is the need for a country-specific approach? What is driving this? Is the leaderboard part of MVRA? We shy away from local solutions unless this is strictly necessary.
** Who from Legal have you been speaking to? Is it someone from GFT, and have they commented on reclass (which Privacy cannot comment on)?
** Re email - Can I see the contents of the email? Who is sending the email (is it the local French entity)?
** Re leaderboard - Can you complete a PPRA, and explain how exactly we would be ranking performance?
* Advise the reporter per the following:
** Do we need prior consent? 
*** No. We can rely on legitimate interest. We can produce a LIA on our side to document this - this would not act as a blocker.
** Are there any specific legal constraints we should be aware of when communicating performance-based incentives tied to the Bolt Car Program?
*** Just because consent is not needed does not mean that other compliance steps are.
*** There is a risk here in terms of both security and intrusiveness. To mitigate this, we should: (i) share limited earnings information; and (ii) avoid sharing it in the body of the email if we can (i.e., use encryption).
*** We should include a few things in the contents of the email, including: (i) a disclaimer; and (ii) an unsubscribe link.
*** We should ensure we have a clear process in place for correcting the earnings figure if it is inaccurate.
** From a legal and compliance perspective, would it be possible to implement a leaderboard-style gamification system for drivers, considering that the ranking would be fully anonymized? Are there any privacy or regulatory concerns we should be aware of before introducing such a system?
*** Advise that this is much more risky as a feature, particularly due to reclass risks. GFT should advise first. If we decide to go ahead with it…
*** We would need to take a lot of steps to de-risk the profiling elements of the feature, including: (i) clear documentation on how ranking decisions are made; (ii) measures to minimise bias risk; (iii) consider alternatives to bonuses; and (iv) offering drivers the ability to opt out.
*** We would also need to make updates to the privacy notice.

h3. 1. *Customer's Own Direct Channels (so-called* *_narrow parity / MFN clause_**)*

✅ *Generally allowed*, provided that:

* The clause only restricts the seller from offering better terms (e.g. lower prices) *on their own website, app, or phone orders*, compared to those on the platform.
* These clauses are known as *narrow parity or narrow MFNs* and can benefit from *block exemption* under Regulation (EU) 2022/720, *as long as they don’t significantly restrict competition*.
* There must be *efficiency justifications* under Article 101(3) TFEU (e.g. protecting the platform’s investment in marketing, search and comparison tools).
* However, if multiple platforms impose narrow MFNs and together they cover a large share of the market, the *exemption may be withdrawn* due to cumulative anti-competitive effects.

📌 *Bottom line*: You can include such a clause, but make sure the market context supports it, and there is a real efficiency justification. Narrow MFNs are *more acceptable* from a legal perspective than wide ones.

----

h3. 2. *Competing Platforms (so-called* *_wide parity / MFN clause_**)*

🚫 *Generally not allowed*, especially if:

* The clause prevents the seller from offering better prices on *other competing platforms*.
* The platform has a *market share above 5%*, or the clause covers a significant part of total demand.
* These are *wide parity or wide MFN clauses* and they are *explicitly excluded from the block exemption* in Article 5(1)(d) of Regulation (EU) 2022/720.
* Such clauses can *restrict competition* by:
** Limiting the ability of smaller/new platforms to attract sellers with lower commissions,
** Softening price competition between platforms,
** Increasing platform fees without losing business.

📌 *Bottom line*: Avoid wide MFNs. They are *high-risk from an antitrust perspective* and are generally *prohibited* unless individually exempted (which is rare and difficult to justify).



h3. Summary Table:

||Clause Type||Applies To||Allowed?||Notes||
|*Narrow MFN*|Seller’s own website / direct channels|✅ Yes, conditionally|Requires efficiency justification and monitoring for cumulative effects|
|*Wide MFN*|Competing platforms|❌ No|Excluded from block exemption, likely anti-competitive|

[Draft material for inspiration - possibly subject to modification to meet the market/deal specifics before sharing externally]

_To begin with, Bolt provides ride-hailing services, but it's crucial to understand that we don't own the vehicles, nor do we employ the drivers. This makes it challenging for us to purchase traditional insurance for these vehicles and their activities, due to complexities in demonstrating we have a true insurable interest. While we can opt for a contingent motor liability policy, the effectiveness of such coverage is significantly impacted by the 4th EU Motoring Directive._

_Under the 4th EU Motoring Directive, all EU member states are required to have an uninsured driver protection scheme. This directive mandates that each vehicle must be insured by its owner, making any contingent motor policy we purchase irrelevant. This is because, in many cases, our policy would be secondary to the primary insurance held by the vehicle owner or driver. Additionally, our contracts with drivers and vehicle owners are structured in a way that aligns with this directive, further complicating the insurance landscape._

_Despite these challenges, we are committed to maintaining a responsible platform and ensuring the safety of our passengers. Which includes, but is not limited to:_
_A thorough onboarding process for drivers, which includes checking licences, vehicle eligibility, and insurance coverage for ride-hailing activities._
_Providing safety advisories for drivers and passengers._
_Using services like Onfido for identity verification._
_Continuous validation of documents, with regular audits by us and local authorities._

_Regarding our insurance policies. Bolt's parent company in Estonia and our various country entities purchase their General/Civil Liability insurance individually, which protects our business against potential damages or injuries we might cause._

_It's important to note that these policies do not extend to drivers or vehicles on our platform, as they are not our direct employees or assets. Therefore, they might not be directly relevant to the concerns of a Bolt Ride passenger._

Hi [~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35], specifying the amount in T&Cs is of course more defensible given that user’s must accept prior to using the service. 

For reference, users see something similar to this in the App when they wish to end a ride. IMPORTANT to note, they have already unlocked the vehicle so disclosing the amount here may not satisfy pre-contractual disclosure requirements as, IMO the contract is perfected the moment the user clicks “unlock“:

!image-20250321-131430.png|width=260,height=457,alt="image-20250321-131430.png"!

Also relevant, an amount can be specified in the “Local Rules“ section of the App. Local Ops should have access to the text here via the Admin panel. If the amount is changed, this should be updated. 

Options in order of defendability:

# specify the amount in T&Cs + local rules + end of ride screen - most defendable
# Specify a range in T&Cs + + 
# Note in T&Cs that the amount can be found in the “local rules“ tab within the App
# Don’t specify an amount in T&Cs. - least defendable.

Whatever approach is taken should be considered against how heavily the feature will actually be used (ie # penalties imposed by Bolt), local consumer law, proactivity of local regulators and Bolt’s reputation in the market both with MM and sister verticals. 

Hope this helps, ping me on slack if not 🙂 
BR,LC

*On a separate note regarding Verifi’s standard DPA:*

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
The Verifi’s DPA is generally compliant with the law but not compliant with our internal standards.

My advice is not to readily accept Verifi’s standard DPAs and continue to push for Bolt’s custom DPA next week, as it's not up to our standards and creates some risks. This is also taking into account the fact that we will share sensitive financial data on large scale.
{panel}

Below you can find the summary of main points of concern for privacy:

*Comparison Table: Verifi DPA vs. Bolt DPA Standard - main risks:*

h4. 
||*Provision*||*Verifi’s DPA*||*Bolt’s Internal Standard*||*Comments*||
|*Sub-processor Authorisation*|General authorisation; 10 business days to object|Specific authorisation; 20 calendar days notification|Deviation from standard. Bolt can accept general authorisation but still require longer objection time. 
Low risk⚪  as Verifi is a trusted and certified provider owned by VISA.|
|*International Data Transfers*|Default authorisation permitted with SCCs included|Requires *specific authorisation*|As all transfer safeguards are present per Swiss, EU, UK law, low risk⚪ .|
|*Audit Rights*|Restricted to reports/certifications that can be requested annually (Art. 3.2)|Does not accept such limitations as standard.|We prefer to have flexibility in how Bolt can audit Verifi.
Medium risk:orange_circle: .|
|*Data Subject Rights Assistance*|General clause; no timing obligations|3 business days notification at max.|Lacks specific timelines, which creates risks for our compliance obligations. 
Medium risk:orange_circle: .|
|*Liability & Indemnity*|Not addressed in DPA (covered in MSA)|Always negotiated separately in DPA|Privacy-specific cap is always negotiated as level of risk, such as fines under privacy laws, is much higher.
*This is high risk*🔴 *.*|
|*Data Breach Notification*|No timeline specified|24–48 hours required|Timing obligations unclear. Bolt always tries to negotiate specific timelines.
*This is high risk*🔴 *.*|
|*Technical and Organisational Security Measures*|No specific measures outlined. General obligation to implement measures appropriate to the risk.|[https://bolt.eu/en/security/supplier-requirements/|https://bolt.eu/en/security/supplier-requirements/|smart-link]|*This is medium risk* :orange_circle:  *as the provider claims to have SOC 2.* Certificate must be checked by infosec for approval.|
|*General risk - document posted online.*|Online documents can be modified without notice to Bolt.|Bolt prefers to have signed copied with privacy clauses.|*This is high risk*🔴 *.*|

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*In short:*

* I have a few quick questions below on the risk profile / dating being shared, just to confirm my understanding.
* *_If none of the data being shared can be linked to specific fleet owners / other individuals_*, then we have no concerns with sharing the data from a Privacy POV.
* *_If the data can be linked to specific fleet owners / other individuals_*:
** We would always push for a Data Sharing Agreement here, as this protects Bolt’s position and ensures we are not exposed to unnecessary risk. This is what I would recommend, and I can quickly prepare one if needed.
** If there is no time to prepare one (i.e., you need to finalise approach within the next hour or so), then it is open to the business to proceed without it, provided that you are aware of the risks.
{panel}

I include further details / context below. Happy to discuss.

----

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*QUESTIONS*
{panel}

# I understand from Slack that instead of sharing phone numbers, we are now only sharing fleet company names and fleet car reg numbers (where the cars are EVs) - is that correct? If so, *_is this information being shared in such a way as it could be linked to specific fleet owners_*?
## (In other words, are we sharing the information as: (a) Fleet Owner 1 owns Company A and Cars B & C, Fleet Owner 2 owns Company D and Cars E & F, etc.; or (b) in Sweden, Bolt has Fleet Company A (with Cars B & C), Fleet Company D (with Cars E & F), etc.?)
# Presumably this data is being shared from Bolt’s local Swedish entity to a Juice entity also in Sweden - is that correct? (i.e., I assume the data is not being transferred internationally?)
# Will we be sharing this data in a one-off transfer, or continuously over the next 6+ months?

----

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*ADVICE*
{panel}

*_If we are sharing this data in a way that cannot be linked to specific fleet owners_*, then we have no comments from a Privacy POV and this can go ahead.

*_If, however, we are sharing this data in a way that can be linked to specific fleet owners_*, then I would recommend that we enter into a DSA with Juice before sharing this data. I would be happy to prepare one (it would take about an hour), but let me know if this is required. This is because:

* Some fleet owners may not be aware that we are sharing their data with Juice in this way. If they were unhappy with this for whatever reason, we would need to be able to demonstrate that we have put enough safeguards in place to keep their data safe when sharing it (e.g., through a DSA). Without a DSA, we would be weakening our position if a fleet owner brought a claim against Bolt.
* A DSA contains important provision to protect Bolt’s position if any of the data sharing resulted in liability for Bolt. If, for example, we share the data with Juice, Juice’s systems get hacked, the fleet owners' data gets leaked and the fleet owner decides to sue Bolt for this (being the company most readily available to the fleet owner), the DSA would contain a pro-Bolt indemnity to allow us to reclaim any resulting losses from Juice. Without the DSA, Bolt would be liable to pay these losses itself.
* It ensures good record-keeping (i.e., if Bolt is ever asked by a regulator which third parties Bolt shares fleet owner data with, we would have clear records to show that Juice is one of those third parties).

*_If there is not enough time to prepare the DSA / get it signed_* (i.e., this needs to start today), then it is open to the business to take a risk-based decision and proceed without a DSA. Overall I do not regard the data sharing here to be high risk given the categories of data, and the risk profile would be even lower if the sharing is on-off. However, this is provided that you understand and are willing to accept the risks I have set out above. If this is the case, I have no further comments and this can go ahead.

When a fleet is terminated from our platform (e.g. due to breaching our TCs) and the courier no longer has a fleet, it is acceptable: 

* To *notify fleet couriers via email*: “The fleet that your courier account was associated with has been terminated from the Bolt Food platform and therefore this courier account has been suspended. If you wish to be connected to another fleet, please contact Bolt’s support team.”
* *For our Support Team to provide the couriers who request it with a list of ‘active’ fleets that have authorised Bolt to share their contact details to couriers.* 

+Important:+ 

* It is the courier’s responsibility to reach out to another fleet.
* It’s for the new fleet to register the courier under their Bolt account.

Had the same issue with {{generate_ar_noise_with_gp()}}. Is not entirely clear which parameters to plug into GP to get some actual signups numbers.

Made some simulations to understand the following

# Resulting Time Series Variance is actually linear to the one you set as a parameter (expected)
# A decent metric to apply to time series is difference between the min and the max of the time series (calculated in signups). This metric develops in a log-manner to the set parameter
## At fixed *lengthscale of ls=30*, the formula to set GP’s var to obtain the desired max-min difference is {{gp_var_param = (min_max_diff/2.5)**2}} (note the quadratic relation)

Here’s the plot demonstrating the relationship.

!Screenshot 2025-03-22 at 21.49.00.png|width=818,height=459,alt="Screenshot 2025-03-22 at 21.49.00.png"!

Here’s the script if we once want to resimulate the results

*Script to resimulate the results*

{noformat}lst = []
for ar_noise_var in np.arange(10, 4000, 50):
    #print(f'Working with Seed {seed}')
    # Creating the dataset
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=seed)
    df = SimulationDF()
    df.set_dates(end_date='2025-03-01')
    df.generate_latent_trend_with_gp(rng=rng, initial_intercept=1100, trend_params={'ls':30,'var':10000})
    df.split_to_android_ios(android_share=0.5)
    df.generate_ar_noise_with_gp(rng=rng, platform='ios', noise_params={'ls':30,'var':ar_noise_var})

    lst.append({'ar_noise_var_param': round(ar_noise_var,2), 
                'min_max_diff': round(df['ar_noise_ios'].max() - df['ar_noise_ios'].min(),2),
                'uplift_to_mean': round(df['ar_noise_ios'].max() - df['ar_noise_ios'].mean(),2), 
                'data_std': round( np.std(df['ar_noise_ios']),2),
                'data_var': round( np.var(df['ar_noise_ios']),2)
                })
stats_df = pd.DataFrame(lst){noformat}

Hi [~accountid:618d2fe286c210006aa6241e] - Hopp is required to complete a background check for drivers annually. The City’s guidance (City of Toronto specifically below but other municipalities have similar language) for Criminal Record Checks is:

----

The City shall deny an application for, or a renewal of a vehicle-for-hire driver and PTC driver licence, and no PTC shall allow a person to act as a PTC driver where the licensee or applicant has:

a) Been convicted at any time of a sexual offence against a minor or a person with a disability under any of sections 151 to 153.1 of the Criminal Code

b) Been convicted of any sexual offence under the Criminal Code in the preceding ten years

c) Been convicted of an offence under the following Criminal Code sections in the preceding five years:
i. 84 to 117.15 (Firearms and Other Weapons)
ii. 264.1 to 286.1 (Offences Against the Person)
iii. 321 to 378 (Offences Against Rights of Property)
iv. 379 to 462 (Fraudulent Transactions, Wilful and Forbidden Acts of Certain Property, Offences Relating to Currency)
v. 462.3 to 462.5 (Proceeds of Crime)

d) Been convicted at any time of an offence under the following Criminal Code sections:
i. 83.01 to 83.33 (Terrorism)
ii. 219 to 248 (Major Offences Against the Person)
iii. 267, 268, 270.01, 272, 273 (Major Assaults or Major Sexual Assaults)

e) Been convicted of an offence under the following Controlled Drugs and Substances Act sections in the preceding ten years:
i. 5 (Trafficking)
ii. 6 (Importing and exporting)
iii. 7 (Production)
iv. 7.1 (Possession for use in production or trafficking)

f) Been convicted of any offence under section 4 (Possession or obtaining) of the Controlled Drugs and Substances Act in the preceding five years

g) Been convicted of five or more offences under Chapter 545 or 546 of the Toronto Municipal Code in the preceding three years

h) Any overdue by-law fines, unless the applicant provides proof that such fines have been subsequently paid.

i) Been convicted of any offence under sections 249, 252, or 253 of the Criminal Code or sections 320.13 to 320.18 (Offence Relating to Conveyances) (Motor Vehicles, Vessels, and Aircraft) in the preceding five years;

j) Accumulated nine or more demerit points on his or her driving record abstract at the time the application for a licence or renewal is made

k) Been convicted of any of the following offences under the Highway Traffic Act in the preceding five years:
i. Careless driving
ii. Racing or stunt driving
iii. Exceeding the speed limit by 50 km/hour or more
iv. Failing to stop for a school bus or when signaled or asked by a police officer
v. Failing to remain at the scene of a collision
vi. Driving while licence suspended

_Source can be found_ [*_here_*|https://www.toronto.ca/services-payments/permits-licences-bylaws/private-transportation-companies-uberfacedrive-drivers/drivers-for-private-transportation-companies/] _under Screening Criteria._

----

For Criminal Record Checks that we receive from Certn (our supplier who provides the background checks), we do not receive any details about why the Criminal Background Check has been flagged (whereas the Driver Abstract portion we can see the line items flagged if any). This is standard for Criminal Record Checks to protect the drivers' personal data from a Privacy standpoint. As such, we’ve adopted a *_Zero Tolerance Policy_* (we believe Uber has a similar policy here). 

Redisclosing would essentially give drivers the opportunity to disclose to Hopp the flags on their Criminal Record Check. Hopp would then adjudicate whether the item is permissible (i.e. not a restricted item per the City’s bylaws). 

Out of the 12,901 completed background checks as of 23-Mar-25, we have rejected 297 or 2.3% of drivers. However, of the 297 rejected drivers, a subset (I don’t have a hard number here but anecdotally from when I review these about 50% of these are due to failing the Driver Abstract portion based on the City’s guidance above and not the Criminal Record Check).

From an operational standpoint, it would make sense to continue the current policy of zero tolerance to avoid having i) Local Ops responsible for adjudicating this given the complex nature and ii) Hopp having to receive and store sensitive PII. However, if this is at odds with Human Rights we would of course want to amend this policy and retroactively review the 297 drivers who have been rejected to get them on the road. 

Let me know if you require any further details (an apologies for the lengthy explainer).

Hi [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] 

In this case, it’s not obligatory to have consent (privacy side) of fleets/fleets POC to be contacted by couriers. We just need to let them know, at some point before we share their info, that their contact details may be shared with couriers for joining their fleet. However, there may be a process to have a list of fleets that may actually add other couriers to their fleet, eg it’s not privacy consent, it’s more operational side.



However, [~accountid:5cca9996e494c810153b1b03] [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] why do we need couriers to contact fleets and not vice versa (as proposed in the ticket description)? 

We already apply *this logic during the courier registration*: courier expresses their desire to join a fleet and informs whether they have a fleet or want Bolt to find this one. In this case, Bolt shares courier’s details with fleets (we do not ask for consent as we rely on another legal basis) and fleets contact a courier and agree together on their employment/other setup. It also makes a process for couriers easier, as they do not need to call 100 fleets asking to be joined.

Given we apply this login for the registration, is there any reclass risk of changing the approach when the fleet is terminated? I also think that if we ask couriers to contact fleets directly, we may lose a big % of our supply.

{noformat}files:
  - pattern: "^\\.github/workflows/.*\\.ya?ml$"
  - pattern: "^\\.github/actions/.*\\.ya?ml$"
  - pattern: "^(.*/)?action\\.ya?ml$"
ignore_actions:
  - name: "^actions/"{noformat}

export PINACT_CONFIG=<your_path>/pinact.yml

* export GITHUB_TOKEN

{quote}*I recommend that customers just use at+qcfg="mtu",800 command to use.* 

The reasons are as follows:

# We have analyzed before that the reason is "ACK message replied by the lwip protocol of rtos is too slow"

There are two possible problems:

One is that *the host computer does not send ack in time.*

And the other is that *Delayed processing of ACK by the module after receiving it*



# Because the usb underlying driver is not open source, we have created the [Case: 07684533|https://support.qualcomm.com/s/case/500dK000004eEOZ/swheroguqcx216qcx216fr100073debug34fae150173rtosusb-11module-ppp-downlink-rate-is-low] for Qualcomm to assist in handling.

Qualcomm tests it with USB1.1 under windows did not find the issue, it seems there is no problem with the module.

There are no optimizations found in the current module{quote}

{quote}The main frequency of EG915U is 500MHz, and the main frequency of EG915Q is 204MHz. From this parameter, the processing speed of EG915U is 2.5 times that of EG915Q.
I think that's one of the reasons{quote}

Hi [~accountid:5b7beab5b8624857f09efff2] 

In most cases, users do not receive a notification when a pre-authorization is released.

This behavior depends on the customer's bank. Many banks do not display authorization releases on bank statements. Some may show the initial authorization but omit the subsequent release. Others provide a separate "reservations" section within their banking app, where customers can view any funds currently on hold.

We generally advise against requesting customers' bank statements, as this is rarely necessary.

Pre-authorizations must be released within 30 days. In most countries, the release occurs immediately. However, we have observed that banks in South Africa often hold the funds for the full 30-day period.

Cheers, 
Marten

Hi Teele,

Could you please double-check the occurrence? As far as I can tell, these cases doubled over the last couple of weeks, and I have only been coming across them over the last few months. It looks like it is being accelerated. Please note such direct actions could have legal repercussions in our market. 

The risks that come with blocking are higher than those associated with _not_ blocking. CS are blocking accounts on the basis of ‘theft’ - when it is actually just a matter of taking an order - without any warnings or educative comms being sent out first. The reclassification risks, as well as the dampening of supply through such measures, pose a higher risk in our market. It’s a reclass-sensitive issue. 

We are not asking ‘theft' to be removed. Rather, what falls under ‘theft' to be reconsidered. As I have previously mentioned to Kevin: _…the suggestion for these cases is an immediate hard-block. In this case, theft and robbery are classed together. I don’t see how collecting an order then re-dispatching is a safety issue - it breaches platform T&Cs, sure, but I don’t understand how it becomes a safety issue. No threat or harm takes place. I think we’re confusing ethics with platform guidelines._

As Kevin highlighted in this thread, it can still become a safety issue over time, which is why it makes sense for it to be considered as that - but to class it under ‘theft’/'robbery' immediately and warrant a hard-block or an investigative block immediately doesn’t make sense in our market. 

Moreover, on a more pragmatic level, the investigative blocks are seldom issued properly, let alone followed up with and then lifted. But from what I can tell this matter is still under review.

Each Envoy upstream cluster resolves an endpoint domain name independently in parallel.

In the case of MS setup, the PoC site uses Envoy NLB domain name in thousands of upstream clusters.

{code:yaml}clusters:
  - name: user-auth
    endpoints:
      - eu-central-1a.node.prelive.boltint.net
      - eu-central-1b.node.prelive.boltint.net
      - eu-central-1c.node.prelive.boltint.net
      
  - name: targeting
    endpoints:
      - eu-central-1a.node.prelive.boltint.net
      - eu-central-1b.node.prelive.boltint.net
      - eu-central-1c.node.prelive.boltint.net

routes:
  - path: /user-auth/
    cluster: user-auth
    prefix_rewrite: /user-auth/

  - path: /targeting/
    cluster: targeting
    prefix_rewrite: /targeting/{code}

We have 3300 Bolt services. It means there are 3300 upstream clusters in Envoy config.

TTL of {{eu-central-1a.node.prelive.boltint.net}} is 60s.

Total query rate: {{3300 clusters x 3 AZs x 2 IP stacks (IPv4, IPv6) / 60s TTL = 330 QPS}}

Straightforward way to reduce this number would be by using shared upstream clusters with remote site Envoy endpoints.

{code:yaml}clusters:      
  - name: envoy-internal
    endpoints:
      - eu-central-1a.node.prelive.boltint.net
      - eu-central-1b.node.prelive.boltint.net
      - eu-central-1c.node.prelive.boltint.net

routes:
  - path: /user-auth/
    cluster: envoy-internal
    prefix_rewrite: /user-auth/

  - path: /targeting/
    cluster: envoy-internal
    prefix_rewrite: /targeting/{code}

DNS resolution will be done only once per each Envoy domain name independent from the total number of Bolt services.

This logic will be implemented in {{synchronizer}} service managed by PINT.

Thanks for the productive meeting last Friday on the topic of *marketing retention periods*.

----

h1. *To summarise the main points of the discussion:*

# Currently, retention periods are only managed for different categories of data in Bolt's external tools. LCM prepared a list of the types of data and applicable retention periods per the tools' limitations - [here|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1D_D9DjAVE8pDZoz8DzuOKd1e3j1sXudjuVk566QZhy4/edit?gid=1761888207#gid=1761888207].
# Not all tools have retention periods established.
# The existing retention periods in the tools are *not reflected in the AWS S3 internal database*, which affects *Looker*. This is a gap.
*→ Privacy advises LCM to ensure that the retention periods in the systems are also reflected in Bolt’s internal databases.*
# Additional point confirmed by Privacy: not all tools are connected to Admin.
→ For example, *unsubscribe in Admin will affect Braze*, but not *Infobip*.
# On a general level, the retention periods established by the tools are *not fully customisable*.
→ To request changes in the retention rules/logic, Bolt must *actively reach out* to the tools with a clear regulatory need. The tools may need to build a *custom solution* to accommodate such requests.
# *Privacy will review the retention periods* and compare them with regulatory guidelines to ensure there is no infringement.
→ Based on the fact that retention is generally max. 2 years in tools (e.g. Braze), for the duration of the user profile, the existing periods should be *adequate on a surface level* for the majority of jurisdictions.
# *Separate point on anonymisation/deletion:*
→ Anonymisation of personal data generally has the *same effect as deletion*.
→ If the data is *irreversibly anonymised and cannot be attributed* to an individual, it is considered deleted.
→ This is particularly relevant for *Behavioural events in Braze*, which are anonymised after a 2-year retention period.
# *User Properties* – question raised by LCM:
→ Privacy did not identify any high-risk data in the User Properties/Events list.
→ Overall, the events/properties do not reveal any sensitive metrics (e.g. user with a disability, LGBTQ-leaning user, etc.).

----

h1. *Next Steps:*

# *Privacy* to analyse the existing retention periods and suggest retention periods *where not yet established*, based on capabilities of the internal tools (e.g. *Delighted* – retention can be set from 1 month to 3 years).
# For *existing retention periods* (most importantly Braze):
→ Privacy to confirm adequacy.
→ If needed, suggest alternatives and reach out to *Braze* to confirm how custom periods can be established.
# *LCM* must ensure that *retention periods established for external tools are reflected in internal systems*.
→ E.g., if behavioural data is anonymised in Braze after 2 years, this should also be reflected in our internal databases.
→ *Suggested: a separate call to discuss this point*.

----

h1. *Proposal: Call Next Week*

*Purpose:*

* *Privacy* to present data retention suggestions and share with LCM to discuss feasibility.
* *LCM* to outline next steps for ensuring retention periods are reflected internally.

Bruno Paskulin has identified that there is a data protection / data privacy consideration for this piece of work. 

Please review the ticket and if needed, then please create a sub-ticket for the Privacy team.

h2.  *Key High Risks Identified by Privacy:*

# Unsubscribe via link only affects one category of comms and one channel.
# Unsubscribe only affects that specific account - even if other user accounts are linked to the same contact details.

----

h3. *Factors Affecting the Risks:*

* *Regulatory scrutiny*:
** → Bolt received a *reprimand from a regulator* after an inquiry clarified that a *single unsubscribe request must unsubscribe the user from* *_all_* *direct marketing*.
** → In response, Bolt already updated its manual CS unsubscribe process.
** → _Note:_ This doesn’t prevent Bolt from offering users the option to unsubscribe from specific marketing categories/channels.
* *Compliance Gaps*:
** *Lack of Transparency Principle*: Users may not fully understand how their unsubscribe is being executed (e.g. doesn’t apply to other profiles or marketing categories/channels).
** *Consent violations*: Based on regulatory interpretation, an *unsubscribe request = consent withdrawal*. This means the process must be *as easy as giving consent* – ideally a *one-click action*.

----

h2. *Preliminary Recommendations from Privacy:*

# Provide users with an *easy option to unsubscribe from all categories and channels* at once.
## Currently, discussed solution is - Communication Preferences webpage, accessible via unsubscribe link, that provides the option to unsubscribe from all direct marketing categories/channels.
# Still allow users to unsubscribe from *specific categories/channels*, mirroring Communication Preferences in the apps.
# To mitigate risk #2 (multiple accounts with shared contact details), give users the option to *unsubscribe all accounts* linked to the same email/phone.

 *Prioritisation:*
Based on alignment with LCM, *the key user groups to prioritise* for this change are: *Riders and Eaters.*

Bolt is not responsible for verifying if a request for apprehension (penhora), that was issued and validated by a Court, is still in effect. That issue is exclusively between the debtor (fleet/fleet owner) and the Court/enforcement agent.

Besides that, Bolt cannot disobey a legally and legitimate request issued by the Court/enforcement agent, simply because the Fleet Owner says that the apprehension order has been lifted. The fleet owner has to bring that claim to the Court/Enforcement agent and, if he is right, the Court/Enforcement agent will give him back the amounts that were apprehended. 

Bolt has no involvement or intervention in these types of processes, other than responding to the Court/enforcement agent informing if any amount is due to the debtor and comply with the apprehension order, by giving those amounts to the Court/enforcement agent.

Hi Karina, thanks for reaching out!

The step to recalculate the price was removed to lower the AHT, as the action was too time-consuming. We decided that if less than 50% of the trip is completed, the trip can be considered as not fulfilled and a full refund is issued. But if more than 50% was completed - the trip is almost completed and the user is getting goodwill compensation for the inconvenience.

Also, if the price recalculation threshold isn’t met, even if the agent will recalculate the price manually, they will get the same result as the rider was charged. That’s why we decided to stick with either a full refund or goodwill compensation.

But I’m up for discussing how we could make this compensation logic better, so if you have more context on why we should bring back the recalculation, or any ideas on how we should change the compensation decision, then please share that!

Bolt operates solely as a platform that connects independent drivers with passengers. Under the law, Bolt is neither obligated nor responsible for verifying whether drivers hold valid increased-risk MTPL insurance. The responsibility for ensuring that all licensed taxi and ride-hailing drivers possess the required MTPL insurance lies with the LTSA - the designated public authority tasked with overseeing compliance with licensing requirements.
Given this regulatory framework, the request for Bolt to assume liability for bodily injuries caused by uninsured drivers is excessive and disproportionate to our role and legal responsibilities. It would impose obligations on Bolt that properly belong to public authorities (the LTSA).
Furthermore, shifting liability to Bolt undermines the existing regulatory system by transferring the consequences of non-compliance from the responsible parties (drivers and the LTSA) to a private platform operator. Bolt cannot be held accountable for regulatory enforcement failures, nor can it assume financial responsibility for damages resulting from a driver’s non-compliance with legal requirements that Bolt has no authority to enforce.

Hi Naomi! We have a different approach to goodwill compensation for safety and non-safety issues, as the problems differ significantly. 

Non-safety issues are minor complaints about the driver's behaviour, the quality of the vehicle, different expectations of the rider, etc. In such cases, we can ease the situation by offering the rider a small value goodwill compensation. However, safety issues are much more serious and we have decided that we cannot value them in monetary terms. In safety cases, we refund the user’s money, but we do not offer any additional compensation for the user’s experience, as we can’t put a price on it, and in some cases, the 2 EUR goodwill compensation could even trigger the customer.

Hi [~accountid:712020:36a81a2e-25b2-4001-b97a-448ab17ddb11] - I have updated the [+*agreement*+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DdFLQVxRHEI1P82NA6WPAVwllgB_A_-JLFbztCplvTo/edit?tab=t.0] based on your comments. 

You will note that the structure and content of the agreement has shifted a bit - this is because of your comment that we are sharing this data with Juice for a specific purpose and Juice will not be able to use the data for anything else - this is fine from my POV, but adjustments were needed to the agreement to reflect this. I have also plugged the remaining gaps.

Given the updates to the agreement, I include my updated advice below.

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*In short:* {color:#36b37e}*Ok to proceed, provided we use the updated agreement.*{color}

* We should *push for Juice to sign this agreement* in its current form before we share any of the data. This is now more important than it was previously, as we need to limit what Juice can do with the data.
* In an ideal world we would also conduct something called a ‘Transfer Impact Assessment’ before sending the data, given that it is going to the USA. However, given the time available, it is *open to the business to  proceed without a TIA* (which we can prepare later), provided it understands the risk. 
{panel}

Further context is below, just for your visibility.

*CONTEXT*

* Given that we are: (i) providing this personal data to Juice for specific purposes (i.e., to add fleets quickly) and nothing else; and (ii) Juice will not be allowed to share data with any other third party, we *need to make sure that the agreement reflects this*. A Data _Processing_ Agreement is more appropriate for this than a Data _Sharing_ Agreement, as it more tightly limits what Juice is allowed to do with the data and makes sure that appropriate safeguards are in place, and it contains provisions that are *required by law*. As such, although I previously said that it was open to the business to proceed without this agreement if needs be, I would now say that it is *very important that we implement this agreement before sharing the data*.
* The USA is not fully considered an ‘adequate’ country to send personal data to in the context of EU privacy laws, and so before sending data to the USA companies (like Bolt) need to make sure that proper contractual protections are in place. This is usually achieved by entering into what is called ‘Standard Contractual Clauses’ - I have included these in the agreement. This is another reason why it is *very important that we implement this agreement before sharing the data* - if we do not, Bolt would technically be non-compliant with the GDPR and could face a risk of complaints / regulatory scrutiny.
* Another step that EU companies (like Bolt) are expected to take before sending data to the USA is to complete an internal assessment known as a ‘Transfer Impact Assessment’, which is effectively a risk assessment to fulfil accountability requirements. I have prepared a TIA for data sharing between Bolt and Juice, which is currently being reviewed by the Privacy Team. In an ideal world, we would finalise the TIA +_before_+ the data sharing takes place - however, I understand that this needs to be pushed forward ASAP, and it is unlikely that the Privacy Team would be able to finalise the TIA today. As such, it is *_open to the business to push ahead with signing the agreement / sharing the data without the TIA_*, although note this would technically expose Bolt to compliance risk for the period between starting to share the data and the TIA being finalised. Provided that we finalise the TIA promptly, this would reduce the risk.

Any questions then let me know.

ROUND(SUM(CAST(co.user_price_eur AS double)),2) AS sum_GMV,

COALESCE(ROUND(CASE WHEN ROUND(SUM(co.user_price_eur),2) > 0 THEN ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (is_current_chargeback OR co.is_current_failed_payment OR co.is_payment_problem) /*OR (CASE WHEN co.refund_amount > 0 THEN co.refund_amount*1.0/NULLIF(co.user_price,0) END)>0.8)*/ THEN CAST(co.user_price_eur AS double) END),2)*1.0/ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.user_price_eur) AS double),2) END,2),0) AS amount_ratio,

COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN bl.business_company_id IS NOT NULL THEN co.order_id END) AS count_business_deactivated, 
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN bl.reason = 'fraud' THEN co.order_id END) AS count_business_fraud,
ROUND(CASE WHEN count_business_orders > 0 THEN count_business_deactivated*1.0/count_business_orders END,2) AS business_deactivated_ratio,
ROUND(CASE WHEN count_business_orders > 0 THEN count_business_fraud*1.0/count_business_orders END,2) AS business_fraud_ratio,
ROUND(COALESCE(ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.payment_method_type = 'business' THEN CAST(co.user_price_eur AS double) END),2),0),2) AS sum_business_GMV,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN bl.business_company_id IS NOT NULL THEN co.user_price_eur END),2) AS sum_business_deactivated,
ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN bl.reason = 'fraud' THEN co.user_price_eur END),2) AS sum_business_fraud,
ROUND(CASE WHEN sum_business_GMV > 0 THEN sum_business_deactivated*1.0/sum_business_GMV END,2) AS business_deactivated_sum_ratio,
ROUND(CASE WHEN sum_business_GMV > 0 THEN sum_business_fraud*1.0/sum_business_GMV END,2) AS business_fraud_sum_ratio,
*/
APPROX_DISTINCT((CASE WHEN co.bonus_amount > 0 THEN co.order_id END)) AS count_order_with_campaign,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.bonus_amount/NULLIF(co.eur_currency_rate,0)) AS double),2) AS campaign_sum_eur,
ROUND(COALESCE(ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.bonus_amount > 0 THEN CAST(co.partner_price_eur AS double) END),2),0),2) AS sum_driver_price_order_with_campaign, 
ROUND(CASE WHEN ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.bonus_amount > 0 THEN co.partner_price_eur END),2) > 0 THEN ROUND(CAST(SUM(co.bonus_amount/NULLIF(co.eur_currency_rate,0)) AS double),2)*1.0/ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.bonus_amount > 0 THEN CAST(co.partner_price_eur AS double) END),2) END,2) AS ratio_covered_by_campaign, 
APPROX_DISTINCT((CASE WHEN is_current_chargeback THEN co.order_id END)) AS count_chargeback_order, 
COALESCE(ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN is_current_chargeback THEN co.user_price_eur END),2),0) AS sum_chargeback_order,
APPROX_DISTINCT((CASE WHEN co.is_current_failed_payment THEN co.order_id END)) AS count_failed_payment_order,
COALESCE(ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN co.is_current_failed_payment THEN co.user_price_eur END),2),0) AS sum_failed_payment_order,
APPROX_DISTINCT((CASE WHEN co.is_payment_problem THEN co.order_id END)) AS count_payment_problem_order,

WHERE co.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)

The signature that we purchased was the *Firma Remota* and it can additionally be supplemented with time stamps.

* Tender signatures: for official tender submissions where the Legal Representative signature is needed. This covers all geographies since it is not linked to a specific subsidiary contrary to the ones we have in Spain and Portugal. 
* Tax filling; The tax team needs to have their official documents signed using .p7m format and we have helped with signing for the last two years.
* Other legal documentation: The signature has also been used to sign appeal documents or self-declarations (often linked to tenders) in the past

* While we initially [+advised+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-43252?focusedCommentId=2918153] that we will require a Privacy Notice for 3rd parties whose data we collect and share with MODA for KYC/AML purposes, we later understood and [+advised+|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C080SRRDB9B/p1738752656824639?thread_ts=1737729594.068889&cid=C080SRRDB9B] that: (i) we won't require consent from those parties; and (ii) we can rely on exception to avoid showing them a privacy notice.
* Essentially, this means that this task is now redundant and can be removed. Of course, we will still have our Driver and Passenger Privacy Notices ready for the funnel opening and launch and in those Notices, we will include a 'catch-all' consent and notice about KYC/AML data sharing, if we were ever required to disclose Driver and Passenger data with MODA.

* Upon further analysis of Taiwan's PDPA, it seems that we are entitled to collect personal data from these persons if _expressly required by law_. Therefore, *if there is a specific regulation requiring the data collection,* {{we will not require consent from these persons, contrary to what we thought previously}} (FYI [@sudipto.das|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U04RDTQ5AJC]).
* In Taiwan [+Article 8 of the PDPA+|https://law.moj.gov.tw/Eng/LawClass/LawAll.aspx?media=print&pcode=I0050021#:~:text=Government%20or%20non%2Dgovernment%20agencies%20shall%20expressly%20inform%20the%20data%20subject%20of%20the%20following%20information%20when%20colleting%20their%20personal%20data%20in%20accordance%20with%20Article%2015%20or%2019%20of%20the%20PDPA%3A] requires Bolt to 'Notify' data subjects about specific information when collecting their personal data (usually in the form of a Privacy Notice). *However, it seems that the PDPA in Taiwan includes an exception* "_where the collection of personal data is necessary for....._ {{the non-government agencies to fulfill their statutory obligation}}".

_To begin with, Bolt provides ride-hailing services, but it's crucial to understand that we don't own the vehicles, nor do we employ the drivers. This makes it challenging for us to purchase traditional insurance for these vehicles and their activities, due to complexities in demonstrating we have a true insurable interest. While we can opt for a contingent motor liability policy, the effectiveness of such coverage is significantly impacted by the 4th EU Motoring Directive._

_Under the 4th EU Motoring Directive, all EU member states are required to have an uninsured driver protection scheme. This directive mandates that each vehicle must be insured by its owner, making any contingent motor policy we purchase irrelevant. This is because, in many cases, our policy would be secondary to the primary insurance held by the vehicle owner or driver. Additionally, our contracts with drivers and vehicle owners are structured in a way that aligns with this directive, further complicating the insurance landscape._

_Despite these challenges, we are committed to maintaining a responsible platform and ensuring the safety of our passengers. Which includes, but is not limited to:_
_A thorough onboarding process for drivers, which includes checking licences, vehicle eligibility, and insurance coverage for ride-hailing activities._
_Providing safety advisories for drivers and passengers._
_Using services like Onfido for identity verification._
_Continuous validation of documents, with regular audits by us and local authorities._

_Regarding our insurance policies. Bolt's parent company in Estonia and our various country entities purchase their General/Civil Liability insurance individually, which protects our business against potential damages or injuries we might cause._

_It's important to note that these policies do not extend to drivers or vehicles on our platform, as they are not our direct employees or assets. Therefore, they might not be directly relevant to the concerns of a Bolt Ride passenger._

Implementing a driver scoring system in a carsharing company operating within the EU involves several critical legal considerations. Here are key areas to address:

# *Data Protection and Privacy Compliance*

* *Personal Data Handling*: Driver scoring systems process personal data, such as driving behavior and usage patterns. Compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is essential. Ensure that data collection is lawful, fair, and transparent.​
* *Explicit Consent*: Obtain clear and informed consent from drivers before collecting and processing their data for scoring purposes. Clearly communicate the purpose and scope of data usage.​
* *Data Subject Rights*: Facilitate drivers' rights under the GDPR, including access to their data, rectification of inaccuracies, data portability, and the right to object to automated decision-making.​
* *Data Minimization and Retention*: Collect only data necessary for the scoring system and establish clear retention policies. Regularly review and securely delete data that is no longer required.​

# *Automated Decision-Making and Profiling*

* *Transparency and Fairness*: If the scoring system involves automated decision-making that significantly affects drivers (e.g., restricting access based on low scores), ensure transparency in the decision-making process and provide avenues for human intervention.​[A&O Shearman|https://www.aoshearman.com/insights/ao-shearman-on-data/cjeu-rules-that-a-credit-score-constitutes-automated-decision-making-under-the-gdpr?utm_source=chatgpt.com]
* *Legal Basis*: Ensure that any adverse actions resulting from automated scoring have a clear legal basis and are not solely based on automated processing, in line with GDPR Article 22.​

# *Non-Discrimination and Fair Treatment*

* *Equal Opportunities*: Design the scoring system to be objective and free from biases that could lead to discrimination. Regularly audit the system to ensure fair treatment of all drivers.​
* *Clear Criteria*: Establish and communicate clear criteria for how scores are calculated and how they impact driver benefits or consequences.​

# *Consumer Protection Laws*

* *Transparent Communication*: Clearly inform drivers about the scoring system, including how it works, the implications of their scores, and any actions they can take to improve their standing.​
* *Right to Challenge*: Provide drivers with mechanisms to challenge or appeal decisions influenced by their scores, ensuring compliance with consumer protection regulations.​

# *Employment Law Considerations*

* *Worker Classification*: If drivers are classified as employees or dependent contractors, ensure that the scoring system complies with employment laws, particularly concerning performance evaluation and disciplinary actions.​
* *Collective Agreements*: Be mindful of any collective bargaining agreements that may impact the implementation of performance-related systems.​

# *Liability and Insurance Implications*

* *Risk Assessment*: Assess how driver scores may influence liability and insurance coverage. For instance, if low scores lead to restricted access to vehicles, consider the implications for both the company and the driver.​
* *Insurance Premiums*: Determine whether driver scores will affect insurance premiums and ensure that any adjustments are compliant with relevant insurance regulations.​

# *Regulatory Compliance and Industry Standards*

+*BACKGROUND*+

* Bolt is exploring sending birthday comms to drivers (i.e.,on their birthday).
** This would involve pulling their DOB from Admin and using it for this purpose.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* Overall risk profile is {color:#36b37e}*low*{color}.
** Only processing DOB information, and the impact of processing is positive. Only possible issue would be with scale / how we are sourcing the data in the first place.
** Even if global in scope, seems unlikely that a DPIA will be required, as it is difficult to argue that this could pose a high risk.
* Purpose = To deepen Bolt’s existing relationship with its drivers.
** Seems to fall under the ‘marketing’ umbrella in the draft driver privacy notice.
** Need to be careful that processing is within drivers' expectations. If we are getting this from ID scans, this might concern some drivers.{color:#36b37e} *If they are voluntarily providing it in another context, then better*{color}.
* Legal basis = Legitimate interest (i.e., in deepening relationship).
** {color:#4c9aff}*LIA*{color} would be worth doing, given the potential scale of processing.
* Transparency - Not mentioned in current driver privacy notice. 
** As such, we would need to include a {color:#4c9aff}*disclaimer*{color} in the email.
* DSSRs - Need to make sure that {color:#36b37e}*drivers can object*{color} to being sent these comms.

+*NEXT STEPS*+

* Ask the reporter to fill out a PPRA, as this sounds like a new initiative. In particular, ask the following:
** In what countries are we planning on launching this?
** What is the estimated go-live?
** Where specifically are we getting DOB data from? Has the driver specifically provided it, or has it been extracted from ID?
** Assuming that this process is automated, will we be using a third party to do this, or via Bolt’s own internal processes?
** Will the birthday comms be packaged with anything else (e.g., marketing materials)?
* Subject to answers, prepare a LIA and disclaimer language.
* Advise the business that we should make sure we are obtaining DOB data in a way that drivers expect, and driver should be able to opt-out of the comms.

h4. SD card OS v0.6.1

Full upgrade steps from OS v0.6.1 (SD) + services v0.5.3 to OS v1.8.0 + services v0.7.0

* disable renting (so we don't wait for user to end the ride before rebooting)
* reboot AIoT (to start from known good state)
* set {{ai_wd_enable/0}} (so IoT doesn't do hard reset if sequence numbers go out of sync: [http://prelive-iot.internal/live/iot/bulk_x2_esim.php|http://prelive-iot.internal/live/iot/bulk_x2_esim.php])
* Install {{liblive555.2025.01.17}} (~20 sec)
* Install {{aiot-services.0.7.0}} (~15 sec)
* Install {{aiot-cron-enable.1.8.0}} (~10 sec)
* Install {{aiot-boot-sd.1.8.0-lowperf}} (~60 sec; make *damn* *sure* it finished installing before rebooting)
* reboot AIoT (trigger rootfs expand before model update has a chance to fail catastrophically)
* Install {{aiot-model-parking.1.0}} (~5 min; max 20 in parallel)
* take photo
* reboot AIoT (services reload during model install is likely to crash ai_runner)
* set {{ai_wd_enable/1}} ([http://prelive-iot.internal/live/iot/bulk_x2_esim.php|http://prelive-iot.internal/live/iot/bulk_x2_esim.php])
* enable renting

h4. eMMC OS v0.8.0/1

Full upgrade steps from OS v0.8.0/0.8.1 (eMMC) + services v0.5.3 to OS v1.8.0 + services v0.7.0

* Disable renting (so we don't wait for user to end the ride before rebooting)
* Reboot AIoT (to start from known good state)
* Set {{ai_wd_enable/0}} (so IoT doesn't do hard reset if sequence numbers go out of sync: [http://prelive-iot.internal/live/iot/bulk_x2_esim.php|http://prelive-iot.internal/live/iot/bulk_x2_esim.php])
* Install {{liblive555.2025.01.17}} (~20 sec)
* Install {{aiot-services.0.7.0}} (~15 sec)
* Install {{aiot-cron-enable.1.8.0}} (~10 sec)
* Install {{aiot-usb-ncm.1.8.0}} (~10 sec)
* Install {{aiot-rootfs-expand.1.8.0}} (~10 sec)
* Install {{aiot-boot-emmc.1.8.0}} (~60 sec; make *damn* *sure* it finished installing before rebooting)
* Reboot AIoT (trigger rootfs expand before model update has a chance to fail catastrophically)
* Install {{aiot-model-parking.1.0}} (~5 min; max 20 in parallel)
* Reboot AIoT (services reload during model install is likely to crash ai_runner)
* Take photo to verify that basic functionality still works
* Set {{ai_wd_enable/1}} ([http://prelive-iot.internal/live/iot/bulk_x2_esim.php|http://prelive-iot.internal/live/iot/bulk_x2_esim.php])

Query from Rok:


{noformat}WITH campaigns AS (
        SELECT
            city.country_code,
            city.id AS city_id,
            city.name AS city_name,
            ttc.test_id,
            fcc.id AS campaign_id,
            CASE WHEN fcc.bonus_type IN('fixed_fee', 'guaranteed_sum', 'percentage_of_ride_prices') THEN CAST (fcc.bonus_data AS FLOAT)
                ELSE CAST(GET_JSON_OBJECT(fcc.bonus_data, '$.value') AS FLOAT)
            END AS bonus_amount,
            CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(fcc.rules, r'"type":"no_of_finished_orders","params":\\{{"min_value":([0-9.]+)\\}}') AS FLOAT) AS no_of_finished_orders,
            TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, ttc.campaign_period_start, ttc.campaign_period_end)/60 AS duration,
            -- ELIGIBILITY
            fcc.bonus_type IN ('fixed_fee') AS is_supported_bonus_type,
            DATE_TRUNC('week', FROM_UTC_TIMESTAMP(ttc.campaign_period_start, city.timezone)) != DATE_TRUNC('week', FROM_UTC_TIMESTAMP(ttc.campaign_period_end, city.timezone) - INTERVAL 2 SECOND) AS overlaps_sunday_midnight,
            GET_JSON_OBJECT(test.enrollment_options, '$.type') = 'manual' AS is_manual_enrollment_type,
            (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ng_public_spark.fleet_campaign_period fcp WHERE fcp.campaign_id = fcc.id) = 1 AS has_single_period,
            fcc.personal_period_duration_seconds IS NOT NULL AS has_personal_period,
            test.rules LIKE '%driver_ids%' AS has_driver_ids_in_rules,
            test.rules LIKE '%target_profiling_feature%' AS has_target_profiling_feature_in_rules,
            fcc.spend_objective IN ('engagement', 'retention', 'peak_hour_retention','peak_hour_engagement','other_retention','other_engagement') AS has_supported_spend_objective,
            LOWER(fcc.name) LIKE '%experiment%' AS is_experiment,
            ARRAY_SIZE(
                FILTER(
                    FROM_JSON(GET_JSON_OBJECT(test.enrollment_options, '$.cohorts'), 'array<string>'),
                    x -> NOT ARRAY_CONTAINS(
                        ARRAY('na_active', 'na_churned', 'na_na_activation', 'na_na_zero_FR_lifetime', 'na_risk', 'na_na_churned', 'secondary_active', 'secondary_churned', 'secondary_na_zero_FR_lifetime', 'secondary_risk', 'secondary_na_activation', 'part_time_active', 'part_time_na_zero_FR_lifetime', 'part_time_risk', 'part_time_churned', 'part_time_na_activation', 'primary_active', 'primary_na_zero_FR_lifetime', 'primary_risk', 'primary_churned'),
                        x
                    )
                )
            ) > 0 AS has_unsupported_cohorts
        FROM ng_public_spark.etl_incentives_supply_test_treatment_campaigns ttc
        JOIN ng_public_spark.fleet_campaign_campaign fcc
            ON fcc.id = ttc.campaign_id
        JOIN ng_public_spark.campaign_tests_test test
            ON test.id = ttc.test_id
        JOIN ng_public_spark.campaign_tests_treatment ctt
            ON ctt.test_id = ttc.test_id
            AND ctt.id = ttc.treatment_id
        JOIN ng_public_spark.admin_system_city city
            ON city.id = fcc.city_id
        WHERE
            fcc.state = 'approved'
            AND ttc.campaign_start >= CURRENT_DATE() - INTERVAL '30' DAY
    )
    SELECT
    *,
        is_supported_bonus_type
            AND NOT overlaps_sunday_midnight
            AND NOT is_manual_enrollment_type
            AND NOT has_driver_ids_in_rules
            AND NOT has_target_profiling_feature_in_rules
            AND NOT has_unsupported_cohorts
    AS is_supported,
    has_supported_spend_objective
        AND has_single_period
        AND NOT has_personal_period
        AND NOT is_experiment
    AS is_eligible,
    bonus_amount > 0
        AND no_of_finished_orders > 0
        AND duration > 0
    AS is_valid
    FROM campaigns{noformat}

# Disable users from renting the scooter (so they don't "steal" it and we have to wait for them to end the ride)

## If 10 minutes have elapsed from initial update notification and the model is still not installed, restart AIoT and try again from step 4

# Set {{ai_wd_enable/1}}

Tested initial protocol on following use case

* “IoT devkit“ MCU sends vehicle state (speed, soc, time, turn) every 100ms on channel 1 to display 
* “IoT devkit“ MCU sends images continuously on channel 10, if BOOT button is not pressed, to display
* Display MCU renders MVP html with provided vehicle state
* Display MCU renders and scrolls image

UART is set to 4608000 bits/s

UART data fragmentation is set to 1024 bytes

Display command TX jitter is ~1 ms with no image upload, ~10 ms while images were sent

Display command RX jitter is related to FPS, which was 1/0.120 Hz with no image upload, 1/0.220 Hz while images were sent

Images are 7kb PNGs, which take ~17 ms to receive at ~ 5Mbit/s, ~100 ms to decode

According to this test it takes 30% CPU to handle 5 Mbit/s of UART data, which could be optimized by reducing 1 copy operation

Sometimes data overflow occurs on channel 10

ESP32S3 might not be fast enough to handle 60 MHz SPI as slave

Display jitter is on the edge of what is acceptable, might mean moving away from direct HTML rendering in the future
